title: Bounded Differential Evolution with 120-250nm Hard Constraints
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining all layer thicknesses to 120-250 nm prevents sampling of the >380 nm regime that triggers phase scrambling, while differential evolution's global search capability will find superior local optima within the physically meaningful thickness range.
design_principle: Hard box constraints preserve quasi-half-wave optical spacing at 1550 nm (Ta2O5 QWOT ≈ 157 nm, SiO2 QWOT ≈ 267 nm). The 120-250 nm bounds capture the relevant design space while excluding thicknesses that cause destructive phase interference.
design_variables: all 20 layer thicknesses bounded to [120, 250] nm
soft_objectives: minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds compatible with standard deposition monitoring
no layers exceed 250 nm reducing stress accumulation
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm for Ta2O5 (n≈2.1) is ~157 nm, for SiO2 (n≈1.45) is ~267 nm; 120-250 nm bounds capture sub-QWOT to near-QWOT regime
expected_advantages: Differential evolution explores design space more globally than gradient methods
Consistent with feedback directive for bounded derivative-free optimization
known_risks: May exclude optimal solutions requiring thicknesses >250 nm
Differential evolution may require more function evaluations
20-layer constraint may fundamentally limit stopband rejection
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 dielectric filter on Fused Silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR bandpass application. All 20 layer thicknesses are design variables bounded to [120, 250] nm. Use differential evolution optimizer with explicit clipping to enforce hard bounds. Evaluate coherent TMM across 1300-1800 nm wavelength range. Score candidates using three weighted objectives: (1) mean transmittance in 1545-1555 nm passband (maximize), (2) mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm stopband (minimize), (3) mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm stopband (minimize). Incident medium is air. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all physically valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directive: enforce hard 120-250 nm box constraints and switch to bounded derivative-free optimizer to eliminate >380 nm phase-scrambling regime observed in prior iterations.
